solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Submarine captain a little unemotional (4)

indicatorNotes.a little: a little of something is only a small portion of it, so just a few letters from inside the next word are taken

blocks.note: letters two to five of this word, ignoring its first letter and its ending

annotation.surface: A description of a submarine commander who keeps his feelings in check.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer sits in u-NEMO-tional. 'A little unemotional' reads as 'somewhat cold', which neatly suits Verne's brooding captain.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Verne's Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.

entries.clue: A few root out items such as wellies (8)

indicatorNotes.out: letters that are out are out of place, no longer in their original order

blocks.note: all eight letters of A FEW ROOT rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone digging up a handful of roots, perhaps in the garden in their boots.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Root out' reads as a phrasal verb, to dig up; here out is the instruction to rearrange. Wellies are wellington boots, the rubber boots worn in mud and rain.
annotation.definitionFit: The category named by example: wellies are one kind of shoe or boot, so they belong to this class of items.

entries.clue: Harry and Sarah turning up with son in tow (6)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, a word that turns upward is read from bottom to top, so its letters come out backwards
indicatorNotes.in tow: something in tow is pulled along behind, so the son's letter trails at the end

annotation.surface: Harry and Sarah arrive somewhere with their little boy trailing along behind.
annotation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a man's name partnering Sarah, but it is the verb meaning to pester, and 'and' joins it to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to harry is to pester and worry someone with repeated attacks.

entries.clue: Desperate desire to live (6)

indicatorNotes.Desperate: someone desperate is frantic and in disarray, so the word after it is thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the six letters of DESIRE rearranged

annotation.surface: A desperate longing to stay alive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desire to live' reads as one phrase; the split comes after desire, and live means dwell, not be alive.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of dwelling: where you make your home is where you live.

entries.clue: Go back and plant again, we’re told (6)

indicatorNotes.we’re told: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the answer is what the words sound like

blocks.note: to sow seed a second time

annotation.surface: A gardener returning to a bed to sow it a second time.
annotation.walkthrough: RESEED and RECEDE are pronounced the same, so the spelling comes from the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tides, floodwaters and hairlines are said to do this when they move back or withdraw.

entries.clue: Outhouse only half finished (4)

indicatorNotes.only half: only half of the word is kept, here the back four of its eight letters

blocks.note: the word loses its first half, FINI

annotation.surface: A builder's complaint that the outbuilding was left only half completed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a half-built outhouse; in fact half of the word finished is literally all that is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an outhouse is a small building in the garden or yard, the kind where tools are kept.

entries.clue: Preparing a vinaigrette perhaps (8)

blocks.note: cooks speak of getting a crab or a chicken ready for the table in this way
oil and vinegar poured over salad; 'perhaps' marks it as one example

annotation.surface: Someone in the kitchen whisking up oil and vinegar for a salad.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one idea, making a vinaigrette; it splits after 'Preparing', which is a definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the kitchen verb for getting meat or fish ready to serve, and the noun for a sauce poured over salad.

entries.clue: Explode in meeting about public school (8)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: a date is an arranged meeting
the famous English school near Windsor

annotation.surface: Someone losing their temper at a meeting about a private school.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is a fee-paying private school, and Eton is the best known.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with the answer the transitive-or-intransitive verb used of bombs and charges going off.

entries.clue: Smart Conservative party making a comeback (6)

indicatorNotes.making a comeback: something that comes back travels the other way, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: a party is a REVEL, turned round

annotation.surface: A sharp Tory party staging a return to power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics next to Conservative, but here it is a celebration, a revel.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: smart in the sense of quick-witted and intelligent, not well dressed.

entries.clue: Beer brewed by chemist’s shop — get it cheap here? (4,4)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes a place, so it stands for the noun by example

indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so the beer is placed next to the shop, after it

annotation.surface: A pharmacy selling home-brewed beer and wondering if it is the place for bargains.
annotation.walkthrough: The beer comes first in the clue but last in the answer. A (car) boot sale is a British market where people sell second-hand goods from the backs of their cars.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description rather than a synonym: the question mark flags that a place full of cheap second-hand bargains is being hinted at.

entries.clue: Husband in great pain (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the husband is placed in, inside, the other word

annotation.surface: A husband suffering terribly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great pain' reads as one phrase; great is ACE, which wraps H, and pain alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dull continuous pain, as in a headache or toothache.

entries.clue: Silent comic embracing a man of the cloth (8)

indicatorNotes.embracing: to embrace is to hug, so the comic's name wraps around the A

blocks.note: Charlie Chaplin, star of silent films

annotation.surface: Charlie Chaplin hugging a vicar.
annotation.walkthrough: The A goes between the L and the I of Chaplin; the two names differ by just that one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'the cloth' is the clergy, and this is a clergyman attached to a chapel, regiment, school or hospital.

entries.clue: Liquid he sipped — good for woolly customers? (5,3)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes what the liquid is for rather than naming it

indicatorNotes.Liquid: a liquid has no fixed shape, so the letters that follow flow into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters of HE SIPPED rearranged

annotation.surface: A man sampling a drink that he thinks would suit his fleecy friends.
annotation.walkthrough: Liquid looks like the definition, but it is the instruction to rearrange. Sheep dip is the insecticide bath farmers plunge sheep into; 'woolly customers' are the sheep.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the woolly customers are sheep, and this chemical wash is made to rid their fleeces of parasites.

entries.clue: Good old Henry’s brought back something for the barbecue? (3)

indicatorNotes.brought back: anything brought back returns the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the henry is the unit of inductance, symbol H

annotation.surface: Good old Henry has returned with something to grill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good old Henry' reads as a cheer for a friend; it is three single letters, G, O, H, turned round. A hog roast, a whole pig on a spit, is a British party staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, marked by the question mark: a pig is the kind of beast roasted whole over coals.

entries.clue: I clear up spilt rum (8)

indicatorNotes.spilt: something spilt is knocked over and scattered, so its letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters of I CLEAR UP rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone mopping up after knocking over a glass of rum.
annotation.walkthrough: Rum looks like the drink and spilt its fate, but rum is the definition and spilt the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A British sense: rum as an adjective is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange.

entries.clue: Coach’s bearing (8)

blocks.note: a horse-drawn coach, or a railway coach
the way one holds oneself when standing or walking

annotation.surface: A sports coach's posture.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive but stands for 'is', joining the two definitions; coach is a vehicle, not a trainer.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a passenger vehicle, horse-drawn or on rails, and a person's posture or deportment.

entries.clue: In agreement about head of church straightaway (2,4)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the phrase goes around the letter
indicatorNotes.head of: the head of a word is its top, its first letter

blocks.note: people who agree are said to be 'at one'

annotation.surface: Everyone swiftly agreeing about who should lead the church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head of church' suggests a bishop or the monarch, but it is simply the letter C, which slips inside AT ONE before the final E.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean immediately, without delay.

entries.clue: First lady beginning to lecture in New York regularly (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: the letter is placed in, inside, the abbreviation that follows

annotation.surface: A president's wife starting to give talks in New York on a regular basis.
annotation.walkthrough: First lady suggests a president's wife, but it is Eve, the first woman.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: spaced or spread at uniform intervals, without variation.

entries.clue: Lock up silver in church (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the metal is put in, inside, the church abbreviation

annotation.surface: An instruction to secure the church silver.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as keeping valuables safe; silver is really its chemical symbol, Ag, from the Latin argentum.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to confine, as a bird or animal is shut behind bars.

entries.clue: Prime minister’s daughter visiting me in Paris (4)

indicatorNotes.visiting: a visitor goes inside someone else's home, so the daughter goes inside the French word

annotation.surface: A prime minister's daughter coming to stay with the speaker in Paris.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay rather than making the daughter the PM's.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Narendra Modi has been Prime Minister of India since 2014.

entries.clue: Souped-up old Rover, one with great power? (8)

indicatorNotes.Souped-up: a souped-up car has been rebuilt and modified, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters of OLD ROVER rearranged

annotation.surface: A tuned-up vintage Rover car with a powerful engine.
annotation.walkthrough: Rover was a British car maker; 'great power' fits the engine but the definition means a ruler.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a lord or ruler set over others, holding supreme authority.

entries.clue: Spots Charlie leaving accident (4)

annotation.definitionNote: plural noun defining a singular mass noun

indicatorNotes.leaving: Charlie is leaving, going out of the word, so its C is removed

annotation.surface: Someone spots Charlie driving away from a crash.
annotation.walkthrough: Spots looks like a verb, sees; it is the noun, marks on the skin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an outbreak of red marks on the skin.

entries.clue: LA heavy found in lake (6)

blocks.note: a heavy is a hired thug

annotation.surface: A Los Angeles thug turning up in a lake, perhaps dumped there.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Found in' reads as a container instruction, but nothing goes inside anything; it simply links wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a stretch of still water cut off from the sea by a reef or sandbank.

entries.clue: Police holding everyone back: English crumble (8)

indicatorNotes.holding: the police word holds the other word inside it
indicatorNotes.back: the word is taken back, read from right to left

annotation.surface: Police holding a crowd back while an English side falls apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Holding everyone back' reads as crowd control; it tells you to reverse ALL and put it inside COPS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to fall in or give way, as a wall or a team might.

entries.clue: Stimulate awareness, might one say? (6)

indicatorNotes.might one say: asks what the word sounds like when spoken, not how it is spelt

annotation.surface: A question of whether one could call something raising awareness.
annotation.walkthrough: INSIGHT and INCITE are pronounced the same; the spelling comes from Stimulate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to stir someone up or provoke them into action.
